contents.detail: §5.2.1, printed p.266. The batch-21 supplier is the intended finite entropy interface, but its raw carrier contains malformed control characters; this item is retained as an unresolved supplier and the source result is not treated as readiness evidence.

contents.name: Proposition 5.19, isometric invariance
contents.detail: §5.2.2, printed pp.267–268. Its simultaneous-isometry claim is represented by the assigned lemma; the exact ID is also claimed by batch 21, so readiness remains escalated for owner reconciliation.

contents.name: Propositions 5.20–5.21, entropy and relative-entropy tensor identities
contents.detail: §5.2.2, printed pp.268–270. The product-basis cancellation used after the Weyl average is proved locally in the partial-trace data-processing item.

contents.name: Proposition 5.22, Klein inequality
contents.reason: Klein nonnegativity and its equality theory are not part of this pair’s planned claim inventory; batch 22 does not rely on it for data processing, SSA, CMI, or the Holevo bound.

contents.name: Proposition 5.28, difference-quotient representation
contents.reason: Watrous uses this representation in the Lieb-concavity route; batch 22 proves its compression inequality and joint convexity by a separate finite resolvent argument and does not invoke the difference-quotient formula.

contents.name: Lemma 5.29 and Theorem 5.30, Lieb concavity route
contents.reason: These are auxiliary steps in Watrous’s proof of joint convexity. The assigned proof uses the explicit negative-log compression inequality instead, so no Lieb-concavity claim is imported or left as a hidden prerequisite.

contents.name: Corollary 5.31 and Theorem 5.32, subadditivity and sum convexity
contents.reason: These are intermediate results for the source’s difference-quotient proof. They are not separately asserted; the local joint-convexity proof supplies its own complete compression and regularization steps.

contents.name: Corollary 5.33, joint convexity of quantum relative entropy
contents.detail: §5.2.3, printed pp.281–282. It supports the assigned theorem statement; the local carrier gives a complete proof by resolvent Jensen and support regularization.
contents.owner_reconciliation: Included through the unique canonical batch21 supplier; not batch22 local ownership. Full assigned mathematical scope retained.

contents.name: Proposition 5.34, monotonicity for mixed-unitary channels
contents.detail: §5.2.3, printed p.283. The Weyl average is explicitly finite and unitary, and the local proof applies joint convexity and isometric invariance term by term.

contents.name: Theorem 5.35, channel monotonicity of quantum relative entropy
contents.detail: §5.2.3, printed pp.283–284. The assigned proof uses the finite Stinespring dilation and partial-trace data processing, with the extended support branch retained.

contents.name: Theorem 5.36, strong subadditivity
contents.detail: §5.2.3, printed pp.284–286. The local proof derives the inequality from partial-trace data processing and the mutual-information/QRE identity.

contents.name: Corollary 5.37, mutual-information monotonicity
contents.reason: This consequence is not a separate assigned item. The pair proves the stronger underlying partial-trace and channel QRE inequalities and the SSA claim, but does not add a duplicate mutual-information monotonicity theorem.

contents.name: Theorem 5.49, Holevo bound
contents.detail: §5.3.3, printed pp.295–300. The exact claim is covered by the finite measurement-bound item, whose current carrier is an exact-ID collision with batch 21 and remains escalated.
